clue.text: Writer given university situation but no parking

indicators.note: but no says the parking letter is left out of the word for the university site

parts.note: a campus is the grounds where a university is situated
P is the standard abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An author lands a job on a university site but finds nowhere to leave the car.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Camus was the French writer of The Outsider; 'but no' removes P from CAMPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a French novelist and essayist, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Small vessel taking post into Caribbean island?

indicators.note: into says the post goes within the island word

parts.note: a cay is a small low island, common in the Caribbean
a pillar is an upright post

explanation.surface: A small boat carrying a mooring post to a West Indian isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat; it is the blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A capillary is the smallest kind of blood vessel in the body.

clue.text: Doorstep deliverer kilometres away in city

indicators.note: away says the kilometre letters are removed

parts.note: the milkman delivers bottles to the doorstep
km is the abbreviation for kilometres

explanation.surface: A doorstep milk delivery made far off in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is a major city in northern Italy.

clue.text: What tourist did to show sadness over endless rubbish piled up

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the sigh above the next piece

parts.note: to sigh is to show sadness

indicators.note: piled up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards
endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: waste is rubbish

explanation.surface: A traveller saddened by litter heaped everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts WASTE to WAST; 'piled up' reverses it to TSAW, under SIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: To sightsee is what a tourist does, so the past tense names what a tourist did.

clue.text: Like ecclesiastical building linked with great saint, cold inside

indicators.note: inside says the cold letter is placed within the saint's adjective

parts.note: Basilian means connected with St Basil the Great, as the Basilian monks are
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A description of a church associated with a famous saint, chilly within.
explanation.walkthrough: St Basil the Great was a fourth-century bishop; the Basilian order of monks follows his rule. 'Linked with' looks like a link phrase but belongs to the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a type of large church, and the adjective describes anything in that style.

clue.text: The head started to lose heart

indicators.note: to lose heart means the central letter is taken away

parts.note: began means started

explanation.surface: A leader becomes discouraged after starting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose heart' drops the middle letter G from BEGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean is informal slang for a person's head.

clue.text: Going to drop duck into cooking vessel without a spicy ingredient

indicators.note: into says the shortened going word is put within the shortened pan
without says the letter A is removed from the pan word

parts.note: a steamer is a pan for steaming food

indicators.note: to drop means the zero letter is left out

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing, O, in cricket

explanation.surface: A cook about to throw a duck into a pot without seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is the cricket score of nought, so it means the letter O, not a bird going into the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem ginger is preserved young ginger root, used as a spicy ingredient in baking.

clue.text: Try to follow the Parisian style of today

indicators.note: to follow means the try word comes after the French article

parts.note: la is French for the, as spoken in Paris
to try is to test

explanation.surface: Trying out the newest Paris fashions.
explanation.definitionFit: Latest means most recent, belonging to the present day.

clue.text: Farewell to what angler has on rod to get fish

parts.note: congé is a formal farewell or dismissal
a fishing reel is fitted on the rod

explanation.surface: An angler says goodbye to his rod and tackle to catch a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The conger eel is a large sea fish.

clue.text: Two boys, both small at birth

parts.note: Nat is a boy's name, short form of Nathan
Al is another boy's name, short for Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: Twin baby boys, both tiny when born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both small' means both names are short forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal means relating to birth, existing from the moment of being born.

clue.text: Old lord in underground plot with friends?

parts.note: pals are friends
a grave is a plot of ground dug below the surface

explanation.surface: An aristocrat of yesteryear buried in a cemetery plot alongside his companions.
explanation.definitionFit: A palsgrave was a count palatine, a historical German nobleman, hence an old lord.

clue.text: The principle of reversibility

indicators.note: of reversibility says the word reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A scientist's statement about the physical law that processes can run backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the answer itself: it is a palindrome, a word that can be reversed without change.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true by a group or person.

clue.text: From what they say, fool swallowed a bone

indicators.note: From what they say signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: a loon is a fool, and swallowed is ate, together spoken as one word

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that an idiot gulped down a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunate is one of the small carpal bones of the wrist, crescent-shaped.

clue.text: What the polite curate wanted to say, being yellowish and pale?

definitions.text: What the polite curate wanted to say
definitions.meaning: in the old cartoon a curate given a bad egg said it was good in parts; what he really meant was that the egg was awful
a pale off-white paint colour with a faint yellow tint, named after shells of hens' eggs

explanation.surface: A timid clergyman, wan and sallow, unable to voice his real opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'curate's egg' is a famous Punch cartoon: served a bad egg by his bishop, the curate politely said parts of it were excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The paint colour is a pale creamy white with a slight yellow cast, so yellowish and pale fits it.

clue.text: Planner gets artist for redesign

indicators.note: for redesign says the letters are rearranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A planner recruits a painter to rework a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for redesign' rearranges GETS ARTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist plans campaigns or long-term courses of action.

clue.text: Impervious to pleas, detain a man falsely

indicators.note: falsely says the letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unmoved official wrongly locks up a man and won't listen to appeals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsely' rearranges DETAIN A MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamantine means unyielding as diamond, so someone like that cannot be moved by pleading.

clue.text: The dogs let gases get into beers!

parts.note: to air something is to let air, a mix of gases, get into it
ales are beers

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone has made the beer flat by letting gas in.
explanation.definitionFit: Airedales are a breed of large terrier, so they are dogs.

clue.text: Drug with power to stop sound of cough

indicators.note: to stop means the power letter comes at the end, closing off the cough sound

parts.note: hem is the throat-clearing sound, a small cough
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A medicine strong enough to halt a coughing fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is cannabis, a recreational drug obtained from the plant.

clue.text: I hand out bread with Mary's pate spread

indicators.note: spread means the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shares out bread together with Mary's spread of pâté.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges MARYS PATE; bread is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A paymaster hands out wages, and bread is old slang for money.

clue.text: Pay rise oddly for new recruits?

parts.note: pay is income

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-placed letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A pay increase handed out strangely to newcomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes R and S from RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Incomers are new arrivals in a place or group, so loosely new recruits.

clue.text: No little energy goes into long story

indicators.note: No signals that the energy letter is taken away

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn
E is the abbreviation for energy, hence a little of it

explanation.surface: Without any spark, a lengthy tale drags on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes E from YEARN; 'goes into' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long rambling tale, a story often of doubtful truth.

clue.text: Like a father being friendly, giving shelter to a bird

indicators.note: giving shelter to says the friendly word surrounds the bird

parts.note: pally is informal for friendly
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A dad who is affable takes in a stray bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bird' supplies two pieces, the article and the bird, which go in together as one block.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternal means of or like a father, and this adverb describes acting in a fatherly way.

clue.text: Insect takes plant leaf — half of it

parts.note: beet is a root plant

indicators.note: half of it says only the first half of leaf is used

explanation.surface: A bug eats half a leaf off a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is an insect with hard wing cases.

clue.text: Shown the way to grasp snake, ran

indicators.note: to grasp means the led word holds the snake within it

parts.note: to be shown the way is to be led
the adder is Britain's only venomous snake

explanation.surface: Someone guided along a path seizes a serpent and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran' is the tights sense, as in a stocking that has run, not running away.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights that have laddered have developed a vertical run, so laddered and ran mean the same.

clue.text: Bluish-grey hat worn by little woman

indicators.note: worn by here places the woman letters within the hat word

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
Vi is a short form of the name Violet

explanation.surface: A small woman wears a hat of a dull blue-grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' reverses the usual sense: here the hat holds the woman, rather than the woman wearing the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid originally means bluish-grey, the colour of a bruise.

clue.text: Revolutionary fighter appearing in public on train

indicators.note: appearing in signals that the answer is found running within the following words

explanation.surface: A rebel soldier shows up openly on a railway journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Contras were the rebels fighting Nicaragua's Sandinista government in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: A Contra was a member of the guerrilla force opposing Nicaragua's revolutionary government.

clue.text: Drink to excess, swallowing river in a manner of speaking?

indicators.note: swallowing says the drinking word takes the river letter inside

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker gulps down a river, figuratively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' puts R inside TOPE after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, a manner of using words figuratively.

clue.text: After party the old city is grim

indicators.note: After means the city comes behind the party

parts.note: a do is a party
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A bleak feeling hangs over an ancient town after a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Dour means stern, gloomy and grim in manner.

clue.text: Man's dance finished early

indicators.note: finished early means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: the valeta is an old-time ballroom dance in waltz time

explanation.surface: A man's evening of dancing ends sooner than planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's' is Man is; a valet is a man's man.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a gentleman's personal manservant, so 'man' is a fair short definition.

clue.text: One on detour that's confused must be put right

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: that's confused tells us the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone lost on a diversion has to get back on track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' gives a letter and stands outside the anagram; only 'on detour' is rearranged by 'that's confused'.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron out problems is to resolve them, smoothing away difficulties to put things right.

clue.text: Hell, say, to make a note of one not C of E

indicators.note: say signals that the word for Hell is taken by its sound, a homophone

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, Hell
to enter something is to note it down in a record

explanation.surface: A remark about damnation recorded against someone who rejects the Church of England.
explanation.walkthrough: C of E is the Church of England; a dissenter is a Protestant outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissenters were Protestants who refused to conform to the established Church of England.

clue.text: Widecombe's Jan gets rid of wife for a cow!

indicators.note: gets rid of says the wife letter is removed from the surname

parts.note: Jan Stewer is one of the riders named in the Devon folk song Widecombe Fair

explanation.surface: A folk-song character drops his spouse in favour of a bovine.
explanation.walkthrough: Widecombe Fair is a Devon song listing riders of Tom Pearce's grey mare, Jan Stewer among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a young castrated bullock, cattle loosely called cows.
